context: Data visualization — textured raincloud plots (half-violin KDE + box plot + jittered strip) for 6 groups with an accessibility-focused dual encoding (color + SVG pattern) and a deuteranopia simulation toggle.
first_impression: A thoughtfully designed, accessibility-conscious chart with a deliberate Tol Bright palette, layered texture encoding, and genuine typographic hierarchy — well above the generic baseline.
what_works: The Tol Bright palette paired with distinct SVG texture overlays is a purposeful dual-encoding choice that directly serves the chart's stated accessibility goal; the typographic hierarchy is genuinely layered — bold title, muted subtitle, weighted group labels, soft legend subtext — giving the eye a clear entry point.
what_doesnt: The bottom row (Fjord) is slightly cropped in the rendered view, with jittered strip dots running into the margin — a layout precision issue that undermines an otherwise clean composition; several patterns (diagonal vs. cross, dots vs. waves) are difficult to distinguish at the rendered dot sizes, which partially defeats the purpose of the dual-encoding accessibility feature.
